highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has announced Claude Opus 5, the latest and most capable model in the Claude family. Developers using Claude Code will want to explore how this new model can enhance their AI-assisted coding workflows, as Opus models typically bring significant reasoning and code quality improvements.

highlights.title: Auto Mode is Now the Default in Claude Code
highlights.summary: Anthropic has made Auto mode the default setting in Claude Code, meaning the tool will now automatically select the best model and approach for your task without manual configuration. This is a great quality-of-life improvement for beginners who previously had to understand model selection to get optimal results.

highlights.title: Message Your Other Claude Code Sessions
highlights.summary: Claude Code now supports cross-session messaging, allowing you to send messages between different active Claude Code sessions. This is especially useful for complex projects where you have multiple agents or workstreams running in parallel and need them to coordinate or share context.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.224: Self-Hosted Runner & Archive Plugin Source
highlights.summary: Version 2.1.224 introduces `claude self-hosted-runner`, which lets Team and Enterprise users turn their own machines or containers into execution environments for Claude Code web, mobile, and desktop sessions. It also adds an `archive` plugin source so you can install plugins from a zip file over HTTPS without needing git, making plugin management more flexible.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.225: Gateway Spend-Limit Support
highlights.summary: This release adds gateway spend-limit awareness to Claude Code's usage warnings — when you hit a spending cap, the message now shows the cap name, reset time, and any operator message, making it much easier to understand why you've been rate-limited. This is particularly helpful for teams using Claude Code on managed enterprise gateways.

highlights.title: Mastering Claude Code in 30 Minutes
highlights.summary: This YouTube tutorial offers a concise 30-minute deep dive into Claude Code, making it ideal for developers who want to get productive quickly without committing to a multi-hour course. It covers key features and workflows that will help you start using Claude Code effectively in your VS Code projects right away.

highlights.title: Agent Skills That Bring Team Coding Standards to Claude Code
highlights.summary: The `adlc-team-skills` GitHub project provides a set of reusable agent skills designed to enforce your team's coding standards and best practices within Claude Code and Codex. This is a practical community solution for engineering teams who want consistent, policy-compliant AI-generated code across all developers.

tips_of_the_day: With Auto mode now the default in Claude Code, you no longer need to manually pick a model — just describe your task clearly and let Claude choose the best approach. Focus your energy on writing precise, detailed prompts instead.

If you're running multiple Claude Code sessions for a large feature or refactor, use cross-session messaging to pass context or results between agents rather than copy-pasting outputs manually — it keeps your workflow cleaner and reduces errors.

Before installing a Claude Code plugin via git, check if the author provides a zip archive download. With the new `archive` plugin source in v2.1.224, you can install directly from an HTTPS zip URL, which is faster and works in environments where git access is restricted.
